problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=1$ for $-2\pi \le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{(4n+1)\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-2\pi \le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2}$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-2\pi \le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2}=-\pi .
$$
